Text:
The adolescent growth spurt lasts {{c2::2 to 3 years::duration}} and proceeds in a fixed order:

{{c1::hands and feet}} → {{c1::long bones of the extremities}} → {{c1::torso}}
Back Extra:
Cue: growth runs periphery-inward — the parts farthest from the trunk enlarge first, and the trunk finishes last.

Why: the spurt is what brings the body to adult size — by its end, muscle mass and bone density have nearly reached adult levels.

Text: Girls finish the adolescent growth spurt by about {{c1::16 years}}, whereas boys typically reach their growth peak by {{c1::18 years}} and generally become {{c1::taller::taller or shorter}} than girls.
Back Extra:
Why: girls enter the growth spurt at an earlier age than boys, so they finish sooner even though boys ultimately grow taller.

Pitfall: finishing by about 16 years ends the growth spurt, not adolescence, which runs 12 to 18 years.

Text: The adolescent milestone called {{c1::menarche}} is {{c2::the first menstrual bleeding}}, and reaching it before the adolescent years is {{c3::not uncommon::uncommon or not uncommon}}.
Back Extra:
Pitfall: a girl who is already menstruating may still be younger than 12, so menarche does not confirm she has reached adolescence.

Why: menarche signals the maturing reproductive system — by the middle of adolescence the body gains the capacity for reproduction, producing sperm in males and eggs (oocytes) in females.

Ex: the other secondary sexual developments of adolescence are enlargement of the external reproductive organs, pubic and axillary hair, vocal changes, and adipose deposits in the breasts and thighs.

Text:
The leading cause of death changes with age:

All age groups younger than 44 years → {{c1::unintentional injury}}

Ages 45 to 64 years → {{c2::cancer}}, not heart disease
Back Extra:
Pitfall: middle adults may already have diabetes or hypertension without knowing it, so a denied medical history does not rule them out.

Cue: rising cholesterol, decreasing cardiac efficiency, and harder weight control mark these years, though proper exercise and a healthy diet blunt much of the effect.
